text:
Jonatan Berggren has found a role in St. Louis that Detroit never quite gave him. The Swedish winger has 11 points in 23 games on about 14 minutes a night, three of them on the power play, and his scoring rate of 2.04 points per 60 sits right around the league average for forwards. For a second-round pick who bounced between the Red Wings and the AHL, that's progress.

None of it looks like luck. He has five goals on 4.29 expected, shooting 13.9% against a league average of 13.4%, and St. Louis has a slight edge in chance quality with him on the ice (51.2% of five-on-five expected goals). His best night came against New Jersey on November 21: two goals in a 9-6 win, one on a breakaway and one into an empty net.

His minutes have slipped lately, down about 1.6 a night over the last ten, with 11.2 against Dallas. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him exiting the zone with possession 62% of the time last season, a small sample of nine games. Watch whether the ice time comes back; the points have kept coming either way.
